notes: Explicit prayerKeys are editorial links for recurring prayer artwork pools. These do not approve artwork and are never inferred from the prayer date by the runtime.

Coverage-first 12 additional museum object candidates (8 Cleveland with archival originals, 1 Met, 3 NGA). CMA composite diptych requires iconographic review. Two CMA Assumption studies and a misassigned Presentation study are retained in acquisition archive only, not counted as direct artwork candidates.

Two Art Institute painted Pentecost records close the source-catalogue zero for rosary.glo3, but IIIF image downloads returned HTTP 403; original image quality is not verified. They are leads, not acquired paintings.

Batch-2 Met original JPEG acquisition produced 35 technically passing source-authenticated paintings; subjects tagged with caution for composites and patron saint identity. No artist/phone-crop review and no production promotion.

Pentecost 3 Commons originals acquired & SHA1-verified. Public Domain Mark / PD-Art is not CC0; per-image worldwide reuse rights not cleared. The Rosary 15-mystery 2-original availability milestone therefore does not mean 15/15 released or commercial-rights-cleared.

Sacred Heart and Immaculate Heart source-pool minima may use clearly captioned symbolically related Christ/Marian masterpiece; that is NOT an exact painted sacred/immaculate heart. Exact-iconographic works remain an independent acquisition/review target.
Stations pool now has related Passion paintings but still lacks individual station-to-painting approval; no painted image should be displayed under an inaccurate station label.

Acquisition batch 38043542975: six new genuine originals retained; four near-monochrome/low-resolution Met candidates and one specific oil-on-copper classification conflict held, never auto-retired or silently counted as image approved.

Tagged all catalogue works with separately namespaced prayer routes, Rosary mysteries, historic novena subjects, liturgical periods and observed source identity; automatic tag projection does not imply liturgical applicability or artistic approval.

Wide devotion batch ingested with exact-vs-symbolic semantic distinctions; generic Virgin and Child paintings are NOT falsely labeled Our Lady of Perpetual Help; Saint Andrew Crucifixion is a saint entry, NOT Precious Blood or Station XI.

Wide Calendar/saints/Scripture pass imported only source-consistent subjects. Saint Andrew Crucifixion is not Christ's Passion; Cézanne's Domaine Saint-Joseph is not the saint; Beheading John the Baptist is not his Nativity; medieval saints are NOT authenticated contemporary likenesses.

Formation source acquisition reconciliation includes Tintoretto/Cranach Baptism, Joos Last Judgment, El Greco Saint Jerome, Mass of St Gregory, and Samaritan; composite altarpiece explicitly held from single-iconographic-match status.

Class-I 2026 first Lent and Laetare Gospel scene originals physically acquired from NGA/Met with individual SHA256, first-party object metadata and strict exact source links. User editorial artwork/crop audit and production release remain pending. Tintoretto's 3811x1686-wide original must be inspected for portrait phone crop or dedicated landscape layout.

Seven source-verified saint paintings acquired; preserve Saint Lucy narrative at Agatha shrine as Lucy only, correct Bari/Myra versus Nicholas Tolentino, and composite altarpiece/young Sebastian representation. Rejected false met-435885 Cézanne Domaine Saint-Joseph landscape. Research only; not curatorial, crop or publication approval.

2026-10-10 multi-day breadth: six new ZIP-reverified Met/CMA CC0 original paintings, including Epiphany x2, John Baptist preaching, two Marian masterworks, St Francis at Cross devotional context. Physically excluded misleading Cézanne Domaine Saint-Joseph landscape. Virgin/Child is NOT the specific Our Lady of Perpetual Help icon; Francis before Crucifix is NOT historical Station XII.

2026-10-10 added Caravaggio The Denial of Saint Peter as real hashed Met source original; eligible for distinct appointed Passion Gospel narrative passages where the actual denial occurs, not all Apostle Peter observances. Crop/rights/curator final audit remain separate.

Research reuse repair: NGA-505 Piero di Cosimo Visitation already acquired. NGA identifies Nicholas of Myra and Anthony Abbot as distinct visible supporting figures; preserve subject Visitation as primary, tag saints for contextual date reuse only.

High-yield physical-original batch: four official Met paintings and CMA Pittoni 1720s altarpiece (distinct identified saints Agnes, Scholastica, Benedict, Lucy, Veronica, Anthony OF PADUA), plus Catherine Alexandria direct scenes. Never confuse Catherine Alexandria with Catherine Siena, or Padua with Anthony Abbot. Composite fields are contextual. Three Met low-resolution leads excluded without upscaling.

Reused already acquired Met-437336 rosary-institution altarpiece, whose Met curatorial entry explicitly identifies St Dominic and St Francis as separate figures. Tags add these as secondary saint contextual uses, not separate portrait acquisitions.

2026-10-11 official NGA Open Data bulk: forty previously unregistered unique source-original paintings acquired (NGA openaccess=1 image-level, strict painting classification and >2500px source), full official artist credits and image SHA256 archived at run 38093287797. Exact 1962 feast/saint/Gospel associations still await comprehensive user audit; contextual, partial and composite subjects explicitly distinguished. NGA website display slugs provisional, museum objectIDs and original IIIF URLs verified.
